name: Track opportunities and decide go or no-go
summary: Every month about 90 tender notices, invitations and private leads reach the business development and estimating group, and each one needs a quick decision on whether to spend estimating time on it. A bid coordinator logs each opportunity in the CRM and downloads documents, a business development manager screens it against the strategic plan, the chief estimator reads the scope and checks estimator workload, and the vice-president of business development makes the go or no-go call at a weekly meeting. Roughly 30% are pursued. The decision is slow when the documents arrive late, regional managers and the surety have to be consulted, or a private lead has no funding yet, and errors here waste estimating effort on bids the company cannot win.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about $1.5B of annual construction revenue, an Ontario head office and regional offices in Western and Atlantic Canada, bidding public and private institutional, commercial and industrial buildings.
baseline.notes: Describes an ordinary year; COVID-19 delayed some public tenders in 2020-2021 (Bird Construction 2021 results). Systems are a CRM or opportunity spreadsheet, public bid portals, email and network folders.

trigger: A tender notice appears on a public bid portal, an owner sends an invitation, or a business development manager logs a private lead or a prequalification result.
end_state: The opportunity is declined, found ineligible, lapses, or is handed to estimating, proposal or P3 teams with a go decision.

volume.seasonality: More public tenders from February to June around the government fiscal year-end; fewer in December and August.

evidence.note: Organisation file demand driver bid-invitations (60-90-130 a month); author's estimate.

surge.cause: spring public tender season around the government fiscal year-end

evidence.note: Same surge as the organisation file sets for stipulated bids; public owners release capital work in spring.

systems.name: Public tender and bid portals (MERX, Bids&Tenders, Biddingo, provincial portals)
Take-off and estimating software with Excel bid sheets
Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)

steps.name: Scan bid portals and the leads inbox
steps.description: The bid coordinator opens the daily notice emails and saved searches on MERX, Bids&Tenders, Biddingo and the provincial portals, and the shared leads inbox. She picks out building tenders, invitations and prequalification results that fall in the company's regions and size range.

error.defect_description: A relevant notice is overlooked in the daily list and found days later or not at all.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; portals named in the organisation file; daily scanning is common practice.

steps.name: Check the CRM for an existing record
steps.description: The bid coordinator searches the CRM opportunity tracker by owner, project name and address to see whether business development already logged the project as a lead, a prequalification or an earlier cancelled tender.

error.defect_description: A duplicate record is created for a project already tracked.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; CRM in the organisation file.

steps.name: Create the opportunity record
steps.description: The bid coordinator types the owner, location, project type, estimated value, delivery model, closing date, site visit and question deadlines into a new CRM record and links the notice.

error.defect_description: Closing date, time zone or mandatory site visit date keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; re-keying between portal and CRM was usual in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Download documents and register as plan taker
steps.description: The bid coordinator registers the company as a plan taker on the portal, downloads the drawings, specifications, instructions to bidders and any addenda into the bid folder, and notes the plan takers list.

error.defect_description: An addendum or drawing volume is missed in the download.

evidence.note: Plan taker registration and automatic addendum notices on bids&tenders.

steps.name: Screen against target markets
steps.description: The business development manager reads the CRM summary and the scope pages and compares sector, region, contract value, delivery model and owner type with the strategic plan's targets. Work far outside them is declined at once.

error.defect_description: A good-fit project is screened out on a misread value or location.

next.condition: outside target sectors, regions or size

evidence.note: Quick screen before opening drawings; decline share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check eligibility and mandatory requirements
steps.description: The bid coordinator checks the instructions to bidders for prequalified-bidder lists, mandatory site meetings, safety certification (COR), bid security and bonding requirements, and whether the closing date leaves enough time to price.

error.defect_description: A mandatory site meeting or prequalification condition is missed and the bid is later ineligible.

control.basis: Owner's instructions to bidders: only prequalified bidders and holders of COR or equivalent may bid (Nova Scotia guidelines 3.1; Oshawa bid procedure)

next.condition: not prequalified, missed mandatory meeting or certification

evidence.note: Eligibility rules from the sources; failure share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review scope, terms and risk
steps.description: The chief estimator reads the drawings index, specifications and supplementary conditions and notes the size, schedule, liquidated damages, self-perform concrete content, design completeness and unusual risk terms that affect whether the company can win at a margin.

error.defect_description: An onerous term (consequential damages, unlimited LDs) is not flagged.

evidence.note: Project and bidding factors (scope clarity, document quality, lead time) from the source; times are estimates.

steps.name: Check estimating workload
steps.description: The chief estimator opens the bid calendar spreadsheet and checks which estimators are free in the tender period and how many bids already close in the same week.

next.condition: large bid or bonding near the single-project limit

evidence.note: Contractor capacity factor from the source; split is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check bonding capacity
steps.description: The treasury, surety and credit manager compares the expected bid value with the single-project and aggregate limits of the bonding line and the work on hand, and says whether the surety is likely to support the bid.

evidence.note: Bonding is a named go/no-go factor; times and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Gather competition and client intelligence
steps.description: The business development manager reviews the plan takers list, past bid results with this owner, the owner's payment record and funding status, and calls the consultant or known trades to learn who is bidding.

evidence.note: Number of competitors and client history are top factors; tracking hit rate by customer and competitor count.

steps.name: Confirm regional delivery capacity
steps.description: The regional vice-president checks whether a project manager, a superintendent and self-perform crews will be free at the expected start, and whether the region has trade coverage in that town.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; regional VPs own delivery resourcing in the organisation file.

steps.name: Score the go/no-go form
steps.description: The business development manager fills in the weighted go/no-go sheet for client, project, capacity, competition, market and risk factors, attaches the notes and puts the opportunity on the next meeting agenda.

error.defect_description: Scores copied from a template without updating.

evidence.note: Weighted scoring before estimating begins.

steps.name: Decide at the go/no-go meeting
steps.description: The vice-president of business development chairs the weekly pursuit meeting with the chief estimator and regional vice-president, reviews the score sheet and decides to bid, decline or hold. Urgent tenders are decided by email between meetings.

error.defect_description: A bid is pursued with a hit chance below the company's threshold.

control.basis: Company bid/no-bid policy: VP business development approves every pursuit

evidence.note: Decision rule from the sources; go share set so about 27 of 90 opportunities a month are pursued, matching the organisation file's bid volumes.

steps.name: Assign the estimating lead
steps.description: The chief estimator names the lead estimator and support estimators, books the bid in the bid calendar and confirms the plan to handle the closing date alongside other bids.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; estimating department structure in the organisation file.

steps.name: Hold the lead and follow up
steps.description: The business development manager keeps a held private lead open in the CRM and calls the owner or consultant every few weeks about funding, design progress and the selection method until it is ready or dies.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; private leads often take months to reach procurement.

steps.name: Record the no-go and inform the owner
steps.description: The bid coordinator records the no-go reason code in the CRM, withdraws as plan taker where the portal allows, and for invited tenders emails the owner or consultant that the company will not bid.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; courtesy notice on invited tenders.

steps.name: Set up the bid folder and calendar
steps.description: The bid coordinator creates the bid folder, enters the question deadline, site visit, addendum cut-off and closing time in the shared calendar, and registers attendees for the site visit.

error.defect_description: Question deadline or site visit date entered wrongly.

evidence.note: Addendum cut-off of 5 or 3 business days before closing from the source.

steps.name: Hand the package to the bid team
steps.description: The chief estimator holds a short kick-off with the lead estimator, and for proposals or P3 work with the proposal or P3 team, passing on the go/no-go notes, risk notes and delivery path.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; mix set from the organisation file volumes: 22 stipulated bids, 5 proposals and occasional P3 pursuits a month.

steps.name: Qualify the private lead with the owner
steps.description: The business development manager calls the owner or the consultant to confirm budget, funding approval, timing, the selection method (invited tender, negotiated or proposal) and who else is invited, and notes it in the CRM.

evidence.note: Client financial capability is a top factor; times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Private lead put on hold
exceptions.description: A private or negotiated lead has no funding or design yet; business development follows up for one to two months before it returns to review or lapses.

exceptions.name: Bonding capacity exceeded
exceptions.description: A large bid would exceed the single-project bonding limit, so the company declines or looks for a joint venture partner.

exceptions.name: Ineligible after screening
exceptions.description: The company is not on the owner's prequalified list or missed a mandatory site meeting.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from notice to go or no-go decision
benchmarks.population: Canadian commercial and institutional general contractors, public and private building work

evidence.note: Author's estimate: public tender periods of roughly 15 to 40 days (ns2017 notes 40-day postings under trade agreements) leave about a week for the decision; held private leads stretch the tail.
Set so that pursued bids match the organisation file's 22 stipulated bids and 5 proposals a month out of 90 invitations.

benchmarks.population: General contractors, public works (United States averages)

evidence.note: Stated as averages observed across the country; older and US-based.

pain_points.description: Notices are found in several portals and re-keyed into the CRM; duplicates and wrong closing dates creep in.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; several portals named in the organisation file.

pain_points.description: Go/no-go decisions wait for the weekly meeting and for regional VPs, eating into a short tender period.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor practice; weekly meeting cadence assumed.

pain_points.description: Few contractors track hit rate by owner and competitor, so the go/no-go score rests on memory.

evidence.note: Survey: fewer than 10% of contractors knew their bid-hit ratio.

sources.title: Bid or No-Bid: How Contractors Choose Which Projects to Pursue
sources.supports: Go/no-go factors grouped as client, project, contractor (capacity, bonding), bidding (lead time, document quality), market (competition) and economy; client financial capability, project risk, profit potential and number of competitors are the top four; three or more red flags mean no-bid; weighted scoring before estimating begins; hard-bid public work 5:1 to 10:1 and negotiated work 2:1 to 3:1.

sources.title: Bid management in construction: what it is and why it decides your win rate
sources.supports: Illustration of 20 estimator hours per bid at $75 loaded ($1,500 per bid); cost per win equals cost per bid divided by hit rate; survey of more than 2,000 contractors found fewer than 10% knew their bid-hit ratio; a bid/no-bid screen on customer history, fit, capacity, competition and risk before opening drawings.

sources.title: How is Your 'Bid-Hit' Ratio?
sources.publisher: Mason Contractors Association of America (George Hedley)
sources.supports: Average general contractor bid-hit ratios: public works 6:1 to 10:1, private bid work 4:1 to 6:1, negotiated and design-build work 2:1 to 4:1; ratios above 11:1 on public work cost too much in estimating; tracking ratios by job type, customer and competitors guides which jobs to pursue.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Public Sector Construction Contract Guidelines (June 2017)
sources.supports: Prequalification of bidders with a published minimum score (often 70-80 of 100); solicitation documents list major subcontractors, bid security, CCDC contract form; bonding recommended at $500,000 and over; subcontracts of $250,000 or more should carry contract security; addenda no later than 5 business days (major) or 3 business days (minor) before closing and closing extended at least 1 business day when needed; late bids rejected; amendments and withdrawals allowed up to closing; withdrawal after opening only for serious demonstrable error within 2 business days; within 48 hours of opening bidders may be asked for safety certifications, other subcontractors and price breakouts; bids over the estimate may be negotiated or re-tendered; letter of award binds the contractor to sign; contract security within 10 days of award; bid security of unsuccessful bidders returned within 30 days; international trade agreements may require 40-day postings.

sources.title: Bid Submission Procedure (under Purchasing By-law 80-2020)
sources.supports: Electronic bids only through the bids&tenders system, late bids not accepted; COR, SOSE or ISO 45001 required for construction bids over $500,000; digital bid bond of 10% of the bid and agreement to bond uploaded with the bid on CCDC forms, verified through a third-party authentication firm; qualified bids, unverifiable bonds and improperly executed agreements to bond are rejected; contract documents due within 10 calendar days after written notice of award; acceptance time limit usually 90 days; performance bond of 100%, or 50% performance and 50% labour and material bonds, on award; only the low bidder's references checked; if the low bidder fails to execute, award to the next bidder and forfeit the deposit. PDF metadata shows the file was last saved in July 2021; the copy opened carries a later revision stamp.

assumptions: The process ends at the go or no-go decision; estimating, proposals and P3 pursuits are separate processes.
Loaded costs and role titles come from the organisation file (1.35 loading factor for salaried staff).

Go share at the meeting (54% of those reaching it) is set so that about 30% of all opportunities are pursued, which matches the organisation file's downstream bid volumes rather than a published benchmark.
The treasury manager's bonding check is added; the organisation file does not list treasury-manager among this process's roles.
Waits are calendar time and include nights and weekends; the weekly go/no-go meeting is the main wait.
No equipment, vehicles or crews are used, so no resources are listed; office roles have no shift pattern.
